title: The Government Gives You £1,000… Then Takes Back £1,250 😱🏠 #shorts
description:
The government gives you £1,000… then takes back even more.

It's the Lifetime ISA. Save £4,000 in a year and the government adds a 25% bonus: £1,000 free, so your pot is £5,000. But take the money out for anything other than a first home (or before 60), and a quarter of what you take out is gone: 25% of £5,000 is £1,250. That's the £1,000 bonus back, plus £250 of your own savings. Your £4,000 comes back as £3,750.

One thing people miss: a first home over £450,000 counts as "anything else", so the 25% charge applies. No charge from age 60, or if you're terminally ill. To buy a first home charge-free you also need to buy at least 12 months after your first payment, through a conveyancer or solicitor, with a mortgage.

The government plans to replace the Lifetime ISA with a new First Time Buyer ISA (no launch date yet); until then, existing Lifetime ISAs keep the current rules.

Sources: https://www.gov.uk/lifetime-isa/summary · https://www.gov.uk/lifetime-isa/withdrawing-money-from-your-lifetime-isa · https://www.gov.uk/guidance/lifetime-isa-withdrawal-charges-and-charge-free-withdrawals · https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6a33c4586422bec01b117765/FTB_ISA_Condoc.pdf

assumptions: No interest or investment growth; the £1,000 bonus has been paid in; the whole £5,000 pot is withdrawn for a non-qualifying reason.
Charge-free: first home ≤ £450,000 (12+ months after first payment, via conveyancer, with a mortgage), age 60+, terminal illness (<12 months to live).

The Lifetime ISA is to be replaced by a First Time Buyer ISA (HM Treasury consultation, June 2026; no launch date); existing LISA rules continue until then. The Autumn Budget may change rules after 23 Oct 2026.

"A quarter" (spoken) = the 25% withdrawal charge; "takes back even more" = £1,250 charge > £1,000 bonus on a full withdrawal.
